trajectory_summary: The agent loaded the IMF gold price data from /root/data/gold-prices.xlsx and used an existing template workbook (test-rar.xlsx) to generate /root/output/rar_result.xlsx. It populated the Gold price sheet with monthly prices and added formulas for log returns and volatilities, then filled the Answer sheet for STEP 1–3 (turns 18 and 23 in the rolling summary). The agent attempted to run a LibreOffice-based recalculation tool, which repeatedly failed (“list index out of range”) and at one point corrupted the output file; it regenerated the workbook to restore loadability (turns 19–23/30 in the rolling summary). The final workbook was saved and present on disk (turn 31), but official feedback shows only partial correctness: gold reserve values and total reserves lookups largely passed, while key volatility outputs (STEP 1), exposures (STEP 2), and RaR% (STEP 3) failed.
what_worked: Saved a final workbook to the required path: turn 31 terminal output lists “-rw-r--r-- ... rar_result.xlsx” in /root/output, and turn 32 states it was saved to “/root/output/rar_result.xlsx”.
Correctly filled the 95% one-sided z-score: rolling summary turn 18/23 set Answer!C3 to “=NORMSINV(0.95)”, and official feedback shows “step1:C3” status “passed”.

Correctly captured 2023 gold reserve values for the countries present in the Value sheet: rolling summary turn 18/23 populated STEP 2 row 12 by referencing Value!… and official feedback shows step2 gold_value passed for Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Greece, Portugal, Spain, Netherlands, and Finland.

Correctly pulled 2023 Total Reserves for countries where available: rolling summary turn 18/23 used INDEX+MATCH with a wildcard header match, and official feedback shows step3 total_reserves passed for Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Greece, Portugal, Spain, and Netherlands.
Correctly replicated gold reserve values into STEP 3 for included countries: official feedback shows step3 gold_value passed for Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Greece, Portugal, Spain, and Netherlands.

issues.evidence: Rolling summary shows Answer STEP 1 formulas set as C4 = 'Gold price'!D14, C5 = C4*SQRT(12), C6 = 'Gold price'!E14; Gold price vol formulas were D5:D14 = STDEV.S(last 3 monthly log returns) and E14 = STDEV.S(C3:C14). Official feedback reports “step1:C4” failed, “step1:C5” failed, and “step1:C6” failed.
issues.cause: The volatility definitions/annualization and/or the exact return/volatility scaling did not match the benchmark’s expected method, causing all STEP 1 volatility-related cells to be numerically incorrect and propagating error into later steps.

issues.where: turns 18 and 23 (rolling summary) / STEP 2 exposure row
issues.evidence: Rolling summary: STEP 2 row 13 exposure formula was set to value * $C$3 * $C$5 / 100 (using the computed “3-month annualized” value in C5). Official feedback shows every checked STEP 2 exposure failed (Austria/Belgium/Denmark/Greece/Portugal/Spain/Netherlands/Finland all “exposure” status “failed”).
issues.cause: The exposure computation used an incorrect volatility input (derived from the incorrect STEP 1 volatility cells) and likely mismatched the expected horizon/scaling for “near-term valuation swing”, producing systematically wrong exposures across all countries.

issues.evidence: Rolling summary: STEP 3 computed RaR% as exposure/total_reserves*100. Official feedback shows RaR% failed for every tested country in STEP 3 (Austria/Belgium/Denmark/Greece/Portugal/Spain/Netherlands “rar_percent” all “failed”), while total_reserves lookups passed.
issues.cause: RaR% depends directly on the exposure (and volatility assumptions); because exposures were incorrect, the resulting RaR% values were also incorrect. There may also be a structural mismatch with the instruction to replicate “volatility” into the STEP 3 table (rows 20–22) before computing RaR.

issues.evidence: The agent attempted /skills/xlsx/recalc.py and repeatedly got “list index out of range”; one attempt made the workbook unloadable by openpyxl (rolling summary turns 19–23), and even an untouched template caused the same recalc error (turn 30).
issues.cause: Broken recalculation tooling prevented the agent from validating computed Excel results end-to-end inside the environment, increasing the likelihood that incorrect volatility/exposure choices were not caught before submission.

outcome_rationale: Official feedback shows major required outputs (STEP 1 volatility cells, STEP 2 exposures, and STEP 3 RaR%) failed across the board despite some correct lookups, so the overall task was not completed correctly.
